examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Magnitude of a Vector Given the Coordinates of its Endpoints
examples.worked_solution:
We have 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=i+j+2k, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=2i-2j+3k.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overrightarrow{AB}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{OB}-\overset{\to }{OA} \\  & =b-a \\  & =(2i-2j+3k)-(i+j+2k) \\  & =i-3j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{AB}| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+9+1} \\  & =\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Given that $c=⟨-1,0,1⟩$, find a unit vector that is parallel to $c.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{c}{|\,c\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,c\,| & =\sqrt{{c}_{x}^{2}+{c}_{y}^{2}+{c}_{z}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+0+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $c$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{c}{|c|} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}c \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot ⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
